transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I'm here because... I just have this constant feeling like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. 

It really hits me during things like staff meetings at work, or, you know, event briefings at my church. I just can't seem to stay in a chair. I always end up shifting around, standing up in the back of the room, or just finding some excuse to get up and move around. It's getting to be a real problem.
Did you experience this kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. I remember, um, back in grade school I was always getting in trouble for popping out of my seat. I'd end up talking over the teacher, or I'd just rush ahead and start doing things before the directions were even finished. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a kid. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Aside from feeling restless, do you often have trouble keeping your focus on tasks or conversations?

No, not really. I mean, if I'm doing my job—like buffing floors or fixing something around the building—I can focus just fine. I don't really lose track of conversations either, as long as we're not sitting around a table for an hour. It's really just the sitting still and feeling like I need to be moving that gets me. My focus itself is okay.
